section.title: Introduction
section.p: The pmMDA project is an Open Source volunteer project released under a very open license. This means there are many ways to contribute to the project - either with direct participation (coding, documenting, answering questions, reporting bugs, etc.) or by resource donations (money, time, publicity, hardware, conference presentations, speeches, etc.).
To begin with, we suggest you to subscribe to the news and forums of the project (follow the link for information on how to subscribe and to access the forums).

section.title: Contributing Tips
section.p: This is a collection of tips for contributing to the project in a manner that is productive for all parties.

ul.li: Every contribution is worthwhile. Even if the ensuing discussion proves it to be off-beam, then it may jog ideas for other people.
Use sensible and concise email subject headings. Search engines, and humans trying to browse a voluminous list, will respond favourably to a descriptive title.
Start new threads with new subject for new topics, rather than reusing the previous subject line.

Research your topic thoroughly before beginning to discuss a new development issue. Search and browse trhough the archives - your issue may have been discussed before. Do not just perceive a problem and then rush out with a question - instead delve.
Take the time to clearly explain your issue and write a concise email message. Less confusion facilitates fast and complete resolution.

section.title: Install Project
section.p: Developers interested to participate to the project must have an account in Sourceforge and install Eclipse 3.0 on their development machine. The next steps install the pmMDA project.

ol.li: Define a JDK installation named jdk1.4 and another named jdk1.5 in Eclipse (Windows/Preferences/Java/Installed JRE) and mapped them to your local installation of JDK 1.4.2 and JDK 1.5.

Define a classpath variable named JDK_TOOLS and mapped it to the location of the tools.jar file located in the lib directory of your JDK installation in Eclipse (Windows/Preferences/Java/Build Path/Classpath Variables).

Check-out the pmMDA project from Sourceforge using the SSH2 method. Directives how to set up such a CVS repository can be found in the Eclipse help. Directives how to create a key and publish it can be found in the Sourceforge documentation. You should check out the project as a Java project.

Retrieve the development library package available under the download files of the project. Create a directory lib in the project, unzip the downloaded file and copy all the librairies files to the lib directory.

You should now be able to compile the project. Some errors can still remain in the test folders. Start the pmMDA application with the provided model and configuration file, generate the artifacts with all the loaded cartridges. Rebuild the project. Now no errors should remain.

section.p: From now you can work and commit your enhancements in CVS. Do not forget to register yourself as developer in the project to receive write access to CVS repository.

section.title: Project Structure
section.p: The project structure was derived from examples we found on the Internet, in particular on the Apache site. The structure could evolve when the project team becomes more sophisticated and the project grows.
The following rules exist for the project.

ul.li: All source artifacts are stored under the src directory. Each project has a seperate tree. The coding style follows the Sun Java coding guidelines. The documentation of the source code uses JavaDoc. Developers are requested to follow these guidelines.
All generated artifacts are stored under the gendir directory. They are not part of the version management.
All documentation artifacts are stored under the docs directory. All documents are either XML based on written using the Open Office Tools. The final documentation is generated with Forrest.
The analysis and design are stored under the model directory.
The compiled classes of the projects are written to classes. The compiled classes of the examples and tests are written to test-classes. They ar not part of the version management.
All libraries of the projects are stored under lib. They are not part of the version management.

section.p: All build activities are realized with Ant. The documentation is generated with Forrest and JavaDoc. The pmMDA Group is a strong believer of programming by contract. The project provides JavaDoc taglets to document preconditions, postconditions and invariants.

Examples of applications are provided to fulfill two major goals. First potential users of pmMDA and the provided frameworks should have examples demonstrating how to use of the provided solutions. Second these programs are used to perform functional tests on the delivered versions. The goal is to provide a stable, easy to use and well documented tools and frameworks.

section.title: Goals of pmMDA Distribution
section.p: The success of an open source is certainly dependant of the quality of its distribution. The following criteria are defined for the project.

dl.dd: The pmMDA binary distribution is available as a binary compressed file. The user can download it and unpack it. A script file is available to start the application. The user does not need to compile, configure or install the software. The execution of the script file starts a running instance.
The project provides extensive documentation available online as a sourceforge project web site. The JavaDoc of the project is available and checked with the DockCheck doclet.

The available examples can be downloaded and installed. A tutorial explains step by step the configuration operations to perform. An Ant script is available to build all the examples. Script files are provided to start the examples upon build. The tutorial also explain these steps.
White papers describing the implemented concepts are available as PDF files.

section.p: The distribution creation is defined in an ant file. The ant file contains all distribution artifacts of all subprojects. The creation action is defined in the main ant file of the project.
